query: Which standardized metrics and adversarial tests best quantify re-identification risk in clinical text, and what acceptable thresholds should govern data release and sharing?

response.query: Which standardized metrics and adversarial tests best quantify re-identification risk in clinical text, and what acceptable thresholds should govern data release and sharing?
response.answer: The k-anonymity and differential privacy metrics best quantify re-identification risk in clinical text, with acceptable thresholds typically set at k=10 and an error rate of 1% for data release and sharing.

results.content: IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA WRIT PETITION (C) NO. Annexure P1 A copy of email dated 28.07.2025 sent by the petitioner to the Respondent no. Whether there was/is litigation on the same point of law, if yes, details thereof: N/A NEW DELHI DATE: 17.09.2025 SYNOPSIS The instant writ petition in public interest is being filed under Article 32 of the Constitution of India seeking an appropriate writ, order or direction to the Respondent to make publicly available the complete data retrieved from the crashed Air India Boeing 787-8 Dreamliner, bearing registration VT-ANB, which met with a fatal accident on 12.06.2025 at Ahmedabad, and to appoint independent professionals to monitor the investigation, as the Respondent’s selective and incomplete disclosure of critical information, coupled with the premature attribution of pilot error while overlooking systemic faults, has resulted in a continuing violation of Article 21 and Article 14 of the Constitution of India.
